A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SketchDeco, with matching authors, core methodology and retained experiments. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary material are readable and support comparison despite retitling and substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative colourisation results, qualitative outputs, component ablations and computational timings in Table 1 and supplementary Tables S1–S2.

after.justification: v2 reports original global and local colourisation benchmarks, palette-size experiments and qualitative component comparisons in Tables 1–3 and the supplement.

M1.justification: The global-to-local pipeline, BLIP-2, colour-name retrieval, inversion, exceptional prompts and self-attention schedule remain. However, v2 specifies Stable Diffusion v1.5 for the local stage where v1 specifies v2.1, and revises the transition-mask expression used for noise injection. These are limited changes within the retained method.

E1.justification: v2 adds indoor/outdoor Place365-small scenes, Danbooru2023 anime and PascalVOC2012 multi-object scenes, substantially broadening evaluated domains. AFHQ-cat/dog and the 15 internet sketches remain. AFHQ-wildlife, evaluated in v1 supplementary Table S2, is absent from v2.

E2.justification: v2 adds T2I-Adapter plus IDeepColor to global comparisons and ColorizeDiffusion, ColorFlow, MangaNinja and Cobra to local benchmarks. Supplementary comparisons also introduce IDeepColor, SDEdit and standalone Scribble ControlNet. DiffBlender and T2I-Adapter remain, and DiSS is retained in Figure S6. Anime-Painter/CounterfeitXL appear as proposed-method variants, not independent baseline rows.

E3.justification: Sketch extraction changes from PiDiNet alone to PiDiNet plus LineartDetector, and the reported local backbone changes from SD2.1 to SD1.5. New local benchmarks use two random masks and shared reference patches. v2 adds DCCW, drops MSE, tests palette sizes 1–5 and evaluates an Anime-Painter/CounterfeitXL variant. PSNR and SSIM already appeared in v1's supplement.

E4.justification: v2 adds palette-size sensitivity analysis and tests local composition against IDeepColor, refinement against SDEdit, and spatial control against text-guided ControlNet. Original prompt, attention-injection, scaling-factor, VQA and solver analyses remain. The SD2.1-versus-SD1.5 ablation and component/runtime analysis from v1's supplement are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation-run counts, explicit evaluation seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 mentions changing random seeds for interactive previews, but introduces no statistical replication or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive local/global benchmark and ablation results. Existing AFHQ global scores also change: proposed-method cat/dog FID values are 56.51/60.90 in v1 Table 1 and 50.31/89.70 in v2 Table 2. Changed preprocessing prevents interpreting these as established same-setting gains or losses. Wildlife, MSE, timing and the SD1.5 substitution result are removed.

T1.justification: The transition-mask definition changes from max(sum of rectangular-mask XOR terms, 1) in v1 Section 3.4 to the plain sum in v2 Section 3.3. This is a non-equivalent mathematical revision, although the PDFs do not establish whether implementation changed accordingly. The principal diffusion, guidance and attention equations remain; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims of training-free mask/palette control, local fidelity, global harmony and efficient consumer-GPU inference remain. v2's conclusion adds explicit compatibility with more advanced foundational models. Its stronger emphasis on latent composition largely restates the composition formulation already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning pixel-space interaction, CSS3 compatibility with pretrained models, colour naming versus LLMs, palette-size ambiguity and domain-specific performance. Existing small-region and colour-vocabulary limitations remain. The new claim that local results achieve best FID and DCCW across all datasets overstates Table 1, which contains counterexamples.

D1.justification: v2 identifies official/HuggingFace implementations, TF-ICON and Prompt-to-Prompt implementation sources, local CFG=2.5, and metric feature extractors. It removes the approximate 30-second runtime and detailed component/comparator timings, while replacing exact AFHQ sample counts with approximate counts. The stated GPU and project-access link remain.

R1.justification: The broad training-free, user-guided positioning remains. v2 explicitly acknowledges Automatic Controllable Colorization via Imagination as an antecedent and updates discussion with MangaNinja, ColorFlow, Cobra and other line-art work. Some earlier editing/composition references disappear, including DiffEdit and Applying a Color Palette with Local Control using Diffusion Models; supplementary Section K elaborates the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around latent composition, replacing the childhood-colouring narrative. Background and ControlNet explanations are condensed, sketch-to-image generation is integrated into the global-stage section, experiments are reorganized around local/global evaluation, and the supplement is extensively restructured.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and replaces the original architecture presentation with an overview and detailed stage diagrams, adding colour-search, interactive-refinement and noise-injection illustrations. Benchmark displays expand substantially. Original attention/scaling ablations are retained, the DiffBlender/DiSS comparison moves to Figure S6 with additional examples, and six supplementary sketch-gallery figures are consolidated into three.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's central validation gap: local colourisation previously had mainly qualitative evidence, while systematic comparisons focused on the global stage. Multi-domain local benchmarks, explicit palette-fidelity measurement and targeted refinement ablations now test the main contribution directly. These gains outweigh the removed timing evidence and inaccurate superiority wording. Those errors remain material: Table 1 gives ColorFlow better Danbooru FID than SketchDeco (94.87 versus 134.54), and ColorizeDiffusion better indoor DCCW (9.73 versus 11.85).
